physical activity is associated in a dose-response manner with a reduced risk of breast cancer, especially in women with estrogen receptor positive tumors.

physical activity in early life is associated with a lower breast cancer risk, and that this relationship is stronger for estrogen receptor positive tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
higher levels of physical during ages 5-19 are associated with a lower risk of breast cancer, especially for ER+ tumor.
higher levels of physical activities during ages 5 to 19 are inversely related with breast cancer risk and this relationship is stronger for ER+ breast cancer.

The main takeaway from our work is that
early life physical activity may be an important determinant of breast cancer risk.
physical activity in childhood and teenage years is associated with a reduced risk of developing breast cancer later in life.
childhood activity may be a critical period for breast cancer prevention.
